findings.summary: Section 2 contains a word the M19 scan bans, and M19 only scans git-tracked files. A verbatim quote of the Hermes row would break the policy test once committed, and running the test before commit would not catch it.
findings.evidence: BRIEF.md:597 reads '| Hermes | Orchestration | Routes work, manages dependencies, context, handoffs, and execution |'. boundary_words() bans 'handoffs' as a whole word. athena_files() builds its list from `git ls-files`, so an uncommitted docs/spec.toml is never scanned. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` would pass during the producer run and fail after the commit. The plan's 'fails without' line itself admits the gap: 'if the file is scanned'. Fix: State the rule in the plan: no quote may contain an M19 word. For Hermes, quote a substring that leaves the word out, such as 'Routes work, manages dependencies, context,'. The substring match allows this. Add a demonstration that does not depend on git tracking: grep docs/spec.toml for the boundary words, or have spec.rs scan the spec text for the same terms (copy the fragment list and cite policy.rs as its source). Show that a planted banned word in an in-memory quote is flagged.
findings.location: Plan, Criterion 6 demonstration and Open questions (M19); BRIEF.md line 597; xtask/tests/policy.rs lines 88-103 and 53-81

findings.summary: M24's defined_tests() only reads tracked .rs files. Until xtask/tests/spec.rs is tracked, the new M33 row names tests that M24 cannot find.
findings.evidence: defined_tests() iterates athena_files(), which is `git ls-files` minus excluded files. A new, untracked xtask/tests/spec.rs is not listed. every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists would then fail on `the_spec_is_valid_against_the_brief`, or would only pass after commit. The plan lists this as an open question but has no answer for it. Fix: Say how the producer runs M24 honestly without changing git state. One option: Athena's verify step runs after the files are tracked; record that the criterion 7 run is done on the committed tree. Or name the dependency in Risks so the producer does not 'fix' it by dropping the M33 row. Do not have the producer run git add, since git state belongs to Athena.
findings.location: Plan, Files: docs/enforcement.md (M33 row); Criterion 7 demonstration; xtask/tests/policy.rs lines 466-474

findings.summary: BRIEF.md headings carry markdown prefixes ('## 1. Vision', '### R1 — Causal investigation'). The 'appears as a heading line' check must strip the leading #s and a space, or every heading fails.
findings.evidence: Grep of BRIEF.md: line 560 '## 1. Vision', line 786 '### R1 — Causal investigation', line 678 '### Stage A — Understand and reproduce'. Fix: Say that a heading matches a BRIEF.md line equal to '#'+ followed by a space and the heading text, within lines 550-865. That keeps an Athena-brief heading from counting toward the coverage groups.

findings.summary: No change is needed in either file. The plan should say so plainly, not leave it conditional.
findings.evidence: xtask/Cargo.toml lines 20-24 already list regex, serde and toml as dev-dependencies. Fix: State that Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock stay unchanged and why, so the verifier does not count them as missing deliverables.

summary: The plan matches the accepted reading: a TOML spec for Olympus sections 1-6, a pure check function using toml and serde (already dev-dependencies, xtask/Cargo.toml lines 20-24), four in-memory negative tests, coverage grouped by the BRIEF.md headings (all 13 headings exist at BRIEF.md lines 560-856), and D111 and M33 as the next free numbers. Two gaps keep it from acceptance. First, BRIEF.md line 597, in section 2, contains 'handoffs', a word the M19 scan bans. M19 and M24 only scan git-tracked files, so a verbatim Hermes quote would pass during the producer run and break the policy test after commit. Second, the new M33 enforcement row can't be checked by M24 until xtask/tests/spec.rs is tracked. Criteria 6 and 7 are therefore not truly shown. The fix is to keep banned words out of the quotes and check for them directly, and to say when M24 is run.
